title: Make locked Hyprland groups follow the theme
head: 81d7a75c2506
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: one finding (test-only): the new handwritten-theme check in test/cli requires the exact value active_border_color, rejecting themes with intentional locked colours and failing when merged with open #12488. Runtime styling and migration: no defects found. Optional notes: default locked inactive border unasserted (surviving mutant), migration test no-theme case unchecked for refresh, scope limit for user handwritten themes / removed theme / user looknfeel overrides.

leads.summary: The new forced theme refresh can strand a user's active wallpaper symlink if the theme image was removed or renamed
leads.consequence: On upgrade after a stock/user theme removes or renames its selected image, the migration re-stages theme/backgrounds but OMARCHY_THEME_SKIP_BACKGROUND=1 bypasses fixing ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/background. The new migration succeeds and is marked completed while the link is dangling, so the shell has no image until an explicit background/theme selection or a later repair. Related open #10731 fixes this exact callee condition, but is not merged; coordinate the fix or heal the link in this migration while preserving backgrounds that still exist.

leads.summary: Removed active user theme silently retains its stale staged Hyprland Lua when this migration is marked done
leads.consequence: When the previous cleanup migration's marker already exists and the user removes the currently selected extra theme, omarchy-theme-remove only deletes its source. theme.name and current/theme/hyprland.lua survive. The new migration exits 0 on the missing source; omarchy-migrate writes its marker and never retries, leaving the pre-upgrade staged Lua active with locked group styling unchanged. Earlier migration 1787481315.sh:15-22 instead re-seeded Tokyo Night on this same state. Consider retaining that fallback or explicitly clearing/resetting stale staged state, not marking styling complete while old files remain.

leads.summary: Late user overrides to unlocked border or groupbar colors do not propagate to the newly assigned locked colors
leads.consequence: A user can set only group.col.border_active or group.groupbar.col.active in ~/.config/hypr/looknfeel.lua after package defaults and the theme load. These later assignments update the unlocked entry, but the new locked entries keep their earlier theme/default values. Hyprland has separate gradient entries, not a live locked-to-unlocked fallback (unlike its text colors); user-customized unlocked groups thus still visibly differ when locked. Either document that both keys must be overridden or implement a late override/fallback mechanism that preserves explicit locked overrides.

leads.summary: A nonempty but invalid theme.name file can stop the rest of the migration queue
leads.consequence: For a theme.name containing only a newline, -s succeeds but command substitution yields an empty name. The -d test succeeds on the stock themes/ directory, calls omarchy-theme-refresh, and theme-set rejects its empty argument with exit 1. Since the runner uses bash -euo pipefail, it neither records this migration nor runs later migrations, repeating each attempt until theme.name is repaired. Likewise a stale '../' style value can pass a directory check and be rejected downstream. Validate the parsed name rather than only -s and -d; a normal name written by theme-set is nonempty and slugged.

leads.summary: If open #8720 merges, declarative unlocked groupbar colors will not color locked tabs
leads.consequence: The other PR's supported [group.groupbar] active_color/inactive_color inputs generate only groupbar.col.active/inactive in later theme Lua; this PR pins col.locked_active/inactive to black in package defaults. Both applied changes therefore yield colored unlocked tabs and black locked tabs, undermining the common themed appearance. Its validator rejects locked color fields today. Coordinate equivalent locked colors in the other PR's allowlist/generator if both land. This is a conditional integration issue, not a conflict between stacked PRs: read-only compare says diverged, and #8720's diff applies to a disposable copy of this head without rejects, though GitHub reports #8720 CONFLICTING against its live base; merged tests were not run.

leads.summary: New migration test passes when the migration wrongly calls refresh with no selected theme
leads.consequence: The no-theme case only checks exit 0, not that the refresh stub's CALL_LOG stayed empty. A plausible one-line regression replacing the -s guard with `{ omarchy-theme-refresh; exit 0; }` still passes all four new cases. Add `[[ ! -s $CALL_LOG ]]` after the first run; also consider an integration case with the real refresh helper. This test concern ranks below the production behaviour issues.

leads.summary: CLI assertions omit the default locked inactive group-border assignment needed by two stock themes
leads.consequence: The new text assertions check the default locked active border and both template values, but never the default border_locked_inactive. Kanagawa and retro-82 supply only active borders, so if a future edit accidentally drops default/hypr/looknfeel.lua:39, those two themes inherit Hyprland's orange locked inactive border while the matching unlocked inactive border remains grey. The current CLI assertions would not catch that omission. Add a grep for the default inactive locked assignment, or a Lua config-value test. This test gap was source-checked, not mutation-tested with the full CLI.

limits: The wallpaper reproducer intentionally uses headless mode to prohibit post-theme hooks; the live migration uses the same skip-background branch, but live compositor display was not exercised. #10731's patched callee was tested in this controlled branch. #8720's merged code was inspected after a patch applied without rejects, but its tests were not run on the combined tree. No tests or program code ran outside review.py.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new handwritten-theme check in `test/cli` rejects themes with their own locked colour and fails when merged with open #12488.

### Handwritten-theme check requires one exact value

The loop requires `border_locked_active = active_border_color,` verbatim in each theme `hyprland.lua` that sets `border_active`. Merged with #12488, `test/cli` fails at dino-dawn, which sets `border_locked_active = "rgb(F2D18E)"`. **Impact:** test-only; whichever PR lands second must change.

**Suggested change:** require each `border_locked_*` key, with any value, only when its unlocked key is set.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 81d7a75 with a one-line theme patch, and merged with #12488)</summary>

# Reproducer: the handwritten-theme check requires one exact variable name

Reviewed head: `81d7a75c25069fedb0eb55da790cd5ed602609fe` (PR #13565). All runs below used a clean checkout, `bash test/cli` from the repository root, a private HOME/TMPDIR, no network and no desktop session. Output is trimmed to the relevant lines; the unrelated `find: '/themes/': No such file or directory` noise that `omarchy theme list` prints without `OMARCHY_PATH` is omitted.

## 1. A theme that sets its locked border to the same colour as a literal

Patch applied to the PR head (Kanagawa's `active_border_color` is `"rgb(dcd7ba)"`, so this changes no colour):

```diff
--- a/themes/kanagawa/hyprland.lua
+++ b/themes/kanagawa/hyprland.lua
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@
   group = {
     col = {
       border_active = active_border_color,
-      border_locked_active = active_border_color,
+      border_locked_active = "rgb(dcd7ba)",
     },
   },
 })
```

```
$ bash test/cli
...
ok - theme templates style locked group borders
not ok - kanagawa applies its active border to locked groups
$ echo $?
1
```

## 2. Merged with open PR #12488 (themes that style locked groups on purpose)

```bash
git fetch origin pull/13565/head:pr-13565 pull/12488/head:pr-12488
git switch --detach pr-13565
git merge --no-edit pr-12488
bash test/cli
```

Actual output (exit 1):

```
ok - theme templates style locked group borders
not ok - dino-dawn applies its active border to locked groups
```

`themes/dino-dawn/hyprland.lua` on #12488 sets:

```lua
      border_active = active_border,
      border_inactive = inactive_border,
      border_locked_active = "rgb(F2D18E)",
      border_locked_inactive = inactive_border,
```

Eleven of the twelve themes #12488 adds set both locked keys: `border_locked_active` to their own literal colour (for example `"rgb(F2D18E)"`, `"rgb(D39A30)"`) and `border_locked_inactive` to their own inactive variable (`inactive_border` or `inactiveBorderColor`). A text search of the #12488 files shows none of them contains the exact strings the check looks for; the test itself stops at the first failure, `dino-dawn`. The twelfth, `far-horizon`, sets neither locked key.

For comparison, the same merge with open PR #9223 fails with `not ok - hackers-1995 applies its active border to locked groups`. That theme sets no locked keys at all, so that failure is a real gap in #9223.

## 3. Suggested check: presence of the locked key, any value

Replacing the loop body with a presence check:

```bash
for theme_hyprland in "$ROOT"/themes/*/hyprland.lua; do
  if grep -Fq 'border_active =' "$theme_hyprland"; then
    grep -Fq 'border_locked_active =' "$theme_hyprland" ||
      fail "$(basename "$(dirname "$theme_hyprland")") styles locked groups when it styles the active group border"
  fi
  if grep -Fq 'border_inactive =' "$theme_hyprland"; then
    grep -Fq 'border_locked_inactive =' "$theme_hyprland" ||
      fail "$(basename "$(dirname "$theme_hyprland")") styles locked groups when it styles the inactive group border"
  fi
done
```

Actual results of `bash test/cli`:

| Tree | Result |
|---|---|
| PR head with the suggested check | exit 0, `ok - handwritten Hyprland themes style locked group borders` |
| same, with `border_locked_inactive` removed from `themes/lumon/hyprland.lua` | exit 1, `not ok - lumon styles locked groups when it styles the inactive group border` |
| same, with the Kanagawa literal from section 1 | exit 0 |
| PR head merged with #12488, suggested check | exit 1, `not ok - far-horizon styles locked groups when it styles the active group border` (the #12488 theme that sets no locked keys) |
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (Hyprland 0.56.2, full Omarchy config parsed with `--verify-config`):
- At the merge-base, the locked active and inactive borders read `0x66775500` / `0x66FF5500`; the PR cites the first.
- After the migration, locked border and groupbar equal the unlocked values for a templated stock theme (Tokyo Night), a handwritten one (Kanagawa), a user theme with only `colors.toml`, and a git-installed theme.
- Locked groupbar text keys stay unset, so Hyprland falls back to `text_color` / `text_color_inactive`.
- The migration exits 0 with no `theme.name`, and with a removed current theme it leaves the staged theme untouched; a direct `omarchy-theme-refresh` there exits 1.
- The PR merges cleanly into the current `quattro`, and its new checks pass there.

**Optional notes:**
- **Optional test improvement:** removing `border_locked_inactive = inactive_border_color,` from `default/hypr/looknfeel.lua` leaves `test/cli` passing (reproducer below), although Kanagawa and Retro 82 rely on it for their locked inactive border. A matching `grep -Fq` next to the `border_locked_active` check would catch it.
- **Optional test improvement:** the no-theme case in `test/shell.d/locked-group-theme-migration-test.sh` checks only the exit status, so a migration that refreshes with no theme set still passes. Adding `[[ ! -s $CALL_LOG ]] || fail "no current theme is not refreshed"` after that run makes such a mutant fail.
- A user theme that ships its own `hyprland.lua` (for example a copy of a stock theme made before this change) keeps an unthemed locked border after the migration, now Omarchy's default gradient; so does a removed current theme. User `looknfeel.lua` overrides of the unlocked group colours don't reach locked groups, which keep the theme's colour. A release-note line may help.

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer for the default-border note (passes at 81d7a75 with the line removed)</summary>

# Reproducer: the default locked inactive border is not asserted

Reviewed head: `81d7a75c25069fedb0eb55da790cd5ed602609fe` (PR #13565). Run with `bash test/cli` from the repository root in a clean checkout with a private HOME/TMPDIR, no network and no desktop session.

Patch applied to the PR head (removes only the default locked inactive border):

```diff
--- a/default/hypr/looknfeel.lua
+++ b/default/hypr/looknfeel.lua
@@ -36,7 +36,6 @@
       border_active = active_border_color,
       border_inactive = inactive_border_color,
       border_locked_active = active_border_color,
-      border_locked_inactive = inactive_border_color,
     },
 
     groupbar = {
```

Actual result: `bash test/cli` exits 0 and prints the same 119 `ok` lines as the unmodified head, including:

```
ok - theme templates style locked group borders
ok - handwritten Hyprland themes style locked group borders
ok - default Hyprland styling covers locked groups generically
```

Why the line matters (source, not re-run on the mutant): Kanagawa and Retro 82 set only an active border, so their locked inactive border comes from this default line. Without it Hyprland uses its own default for `group:col.border_locked_inactive`, `0x66ff5500` (Hyprland 0.56.2 `src/config/values/ConfigValues.cpp`, the `group:col.border_locked_inactive` entry). At the merge-base, parsing the full Omarchy config with Hyprland 0.56.2 (`Hyprland --verify-config` plus `hl.get_config`) reports `group:col.border_locked_inactive = {0x66FF5500}` for Tokyo Night; at the PR head after the migration, Kanagawa reports `{0xAA595959}`, the default inactive colour.

Suggested assertion, next to the existing `border_locked_active` check:

```bash
grep -Fq 'border_locked_inactive = inactive_border_color,' "$ROOT/default/hypr/looknfeel.lua" ||
  fail "default locked groups inherit the inactive border"
```

The string occurs exactly once in `default/hypr/looknfeel.lua` at the PR head (line 39).
</details>
